title: 72 Hands to Make One Bowl — Jingdezhen Porcelain | China Travel Expert
description:
One porcelain bowl passes through 72 pairs of hands before it's finished. Would you have the patience?

This is Jingdezhen (景德镇), China's "porcelain capital," a town that has made essentially one thing — porcelain — for over a thousand years. The Ming-dynasty science text Tiangong Kaiwu recorded it plainly: "过手七十二，方克成器" — 72 hands to complete a single piece. Clay, throwing, painting, glazing, firing: no one artisan makes the whole bowl, an assembly line centuries before factories existed.

🧭 Expert Tip: Skip the souvenir stalls and head to the Taoxichuan (陶溪川) creative district, where returning young makers throw and paint by hand — best on a weekday when the studios are open and calm.

一只碗，过手七十二，才成器——你有这份耐心吗？
